thread:
Managed MongoDB Hosting: When to Use It, and When Not To

Quick thread 🧵
Managed MongoDB hosting is the MongoDB engine run as a service: provisioned, patched, locked to your app server's IP, and backed up, with a connection string you drop into an environment variable.
Reach for MongoDB when your data is genuinely document-shaped, like content, catalogs with varying fields, or event and activity logs.
For most apps built around relationships and joins, a relational database like Postgres or MySQL is the better default.
Think of it as a MongoDB Atlas alternative you run on infrastructure you control.
